name: Fluticasone (inhaled)
mechanism: Potent synthetic corticosteroid - anti-inflammatory action by suppressing inflammatory cells (eosinophils, mast cells), reducing airway hyperresponsiveness, decreasing mucus production, increasing beta-2 receptor expression
dosing: Asthma adults: Start 100-500mcg BD (MDI/DPI). Maintenance 100-1000mcg BD depending on severity. Children 4-16y: 50-200mcg BD. Available as Flixotide (various devices - Accuhaler/Evohaler), Flovent. Also in combination with salmeterol (Seretide). Take after bronchodilator. Rinse mouth after
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not for acute asthma/status asthmaticus or primary treatment of status asthmaticus. Caution: active/quiescent TB, fungal infections, severe hepatic impairment (↑ systemic exposure)
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, ketoconazole, itraconazole) ↑ systemic exposure - avoid strong inhibitors or use lowest ICS dose. May interact with other potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (cobicistat, clarithromycin). Risk of Cushing's syndrome with strong inhibitors
monitoring: Peak flow/spirometry (baseline, 4-8 weeks, then as needed). Symptom control (day/night), SABA use (<3x/week if controlled), exacerbations. Inhaler technique (every visit). Growth in children (annual height). Signs of oral candidiasis. Adrenal suppression with high doses (morning cortisol if >500mcg/day >3 months). Bone density if very high dose long-term
pregnancy: Safe - benefits outweigh risks. Poorly controlled asthma greater risk to mother/fetus than ICS. Continue if controlling asthma. Beclometasone has most pregnancy data, but fluticasone widely used and considered safe. Monitor asthma closely as may worsen/improve in pregnancy
sideEffects: Common: oral candidiasis (10% - rinse mouth after use), hoarse voice/dysphonia, throat irritation, cough. Uncommon: paradoxical bronchospasm (rare - stop if occurs). High doses/prolonged use: adrenal suppression (very rare, reversible), growth retardation in children (monitor height), osteoporosis (very high dose), cataracts, glaucoma, psychiatric effects, bruising. Systemic effects more likely with doses >500mcg/day
pharmacokinetics: Inhaled route. ~10-30% reaches lungs (rest deposited in oropharynx, swallowed). Minimal systemic absorption (<1% from lungs). Swallowed portion undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism. Half-life: 7.8h. Metabolized by CYP3A4. Twice daily dosing maintains effect
clinicalPearls: Higher potency than beclometasone/budesonide mcg-for-mcg (100mcg fluticasone ≈ 200-250mcg beclometasone). MUST rinse mouth and spit after use (reduces candidiasis/dysphonia). Not a reliever - patients need SABA for acute symptoms. Start at dose appropriate for severity then step down after 3 months if stable. Often combined with LABA (salmeterol in Seretide - never use LABA alone). Multiple devices available - Accuhaler (DPI, breath-actuated), Evohaler (MDI, may need spacer). Check technique: common errors include not breathing out first, not breath-holding 10 seconds, wrong inspiratory effort. Step up if using SABA >3x/week, nocturnal waking, or exacerbations. Step down by 25-50% every 3 months if stable. For high-dose ICS (>500mcg/day), consider adding LABA/LAMA/LTRA before increasing further. In children, monitor growth closely - if growth falters, review need or consider alternative
indication: Asthma (prophylaxis and maintenance therapy, not for acute relief), COPD (in selected cases - usually with LABA)
